Figure 2:Lifting a pretrained latent video DiT to pixel space.Top:the pretrained latent model.
A linear pixel-latent alignment, fitted offline, is fused with the pretrained patch embedding to obtain a pixel patch embedding.Bottom:PixVid.
A timestep calibration rescales noisy pixel input to the signal-to-noise ratio the pretrained DiT was trained on.
The DiT is initialized from the latent model, and a convolutional detailer head replaces the linear head and VAE decoder to predict the clean video directly.

A new up blockL+1L{+}1is prepended to the detailer head and initialized as nearest neighbor upsampling. With token count unchanged, we train at2×2{\times}resolution
at the same DiT cost.
Figure 5:Depth-conditioned Editing.Our pixel model enables precise video editing under high motion, while the temporally compressed latent model morphs and blurs fast-moving objects.

Figure 6:Control-to-screen latency.Control inputs,e.g.turn right (→\rightarrow), turn left (←\leftarrow), and look down (↓\downarrow), arrive over time (top row). Colors indicate which control each generated frame reflects.Latent model:controls are reflected in the next block. With block sizeNNthis means a wait of up toN−1N-1frames. We useN=4N=4for this visualization.Pixel model (ours):generates one frame per control, so controls are reflected with zero wait, making it better suited for real-time interactive generation.

Figure 7:Responsiveness.SolarWM receives one pose per four-frame latent, resulting in inaccurate motion when the direction changes; here continuing to look up when it should look down. PixVid handles direction changes natively.

Figure 8:Impact of output head.Under𝒙\bm{x}-prediction, a linear head maps each DiT token to its pixel patch independently, causing visible grid-like artifacts, while our convolutional head removes most seams. Metric details are in App.B.6.

Figure 9:Impact of prediction target.With the same convolutional head,𝒗\bm{v}-prediction produces grainy frames at80×80\timesthe estimated noise of𝒙\bm{x}-prediction, while𝒙\bm{x}-prediction produces clean ones. Metric details are in App.B.6.

Figure 10:Sampler-state precision.We use the same prompt and initial noise in every column. With a bf16 sampler state, UniPC drains pixel-space sample color (red), while Euler keeps it.Color keptis mean OKLab chroma relative to an fp32 sampler state.

Figure 12:Comparison with One-latent SolarWM.SolarWM and PixVid show relatively small motion errors and produce moderately realistic videos. In contrast, One-latent SolarWM follows the controls less closely, here severely overestimating the motion, and looks less realistic.

Figure 15:High-Resolution Video Generation.Left:text-to-video samples generated by our pixel model at a resolution of1664×9601664\times 960.Right:native-resolution crops of the boxed regions. Our method preserves fine pixel-level details such as fur, whiskers and architectural details because the model directly generates pixels without a VAE that compresses and reconstructs them.
Figure 16:Depth-to-video comparison on fast motion.PixVid can generate high-quality outputs under sharp and fast motion.
